task.title: Benchmark the agent hot loop and the sync watcher steady state
task.description:
The benchmark harness covers 33 scenarios but misses the path agents actually hammer and the process beta users will leave running.

No scenario measures `workbook next` or `workbook show`. Neither appears in the registry (internal/perf/registry.go:8-42). This is the loop an agent runs continuously: next to acquire work, show to read context, update to record progress. Only update is measured. It matters more than the omission suggests, because next fetches before answering so two agents do not claim the same task (internal/cli/run.go:735 writes a synced result with a sync report), which plausibly puts it in the autosync latency class near 700 ms rather than the local class near 200 ms. That is not inferable from cli-list or cli-update, and it is the single most likely user-visible latency surprise in agent-driven use.

No scenario measures the watcher steady state. cli-update-watched runs a watcher configured with a one-hour interval precisely so it never syncs during the sample (internal/perf/scenarios.go:290-317), which measures the mutation hand-off and deliberately not the daemon. Nothing samples CPU or resident memory of `workbook sync --watch` over time, or the cost of one sync tick at a realistic interval. Every tick calls Repository.Sync, whose fetch reads every canonical and tracking tip into maps and whose Push re-reads every tip, all through the fully buffering runGitWithEnvResult, so per-tick allocation scales with total task count even when nothing changed. Beta users will run this daemon for hours.

No read-side web measurement. api-update and the two API bursts measure mutations against a populated board, but the GET side is untimed setup only (internal/perf/scenarios.go:1192-1237): no board page load, no /api/tasks read, no task detail, no history endpoint. Worth noting the existing api-update p95 target of 100 ms has been missed in every evidence set since 2026-07-29 (README:75-76, 120, 156), which is already tracked but deserves a decision before beta.

Acceptance:
- Scenarios exist for cli-next and cli-show at the standard acceptance fixture, with duration targets chosen deliberately and the sync behavior of next accounted for in the target rather than hidden by it.
- A watcher steady-state scenario reports CPU and peak resident memory over a bounded observation window at a realistic interval, and reports per-tick cost with no changes pending.
- At least one warm read scenario measures GET /api/tasks against the populated board.
- Evidence is recorded for both object formats under docs/performance/ following the documented process.
- The standing api-update target miss is either resolved or explicitly re-approved with a new target before beta.

Depends on nothing, but coordinate with the validation bounding work so both re-measure against the same fixture points.
